The Present Application U/S. 12 Of The ... vs Unknown on 11
February, 2010
 1
 In The Court Of Ms. Veena Rani
 Metropolitan Magistrate
Patiala House Courts, New Delhi.

In Re :412/1 ( Date of filing :25-09-2009)
Megha Modani v. Piyush Modani &
 others.
 Complaint under the Protection of women from Domestic
 Violence Act, 2005
 P.S.- Hauz
 Khaas.
 The Order

1. The present application u/s. 12 of the Protection of women  from Domestic Violence Act, 2005 has been filed on  23.09.2009 by Ms. Megha Modani (the applicant-wife)
 against : Sh. Piyush Modani (husband as R-1); Smt. Jayshree  Modani (mother-in-law as R-2); Smt. Ritu Kuchhal (sister-in-  law as R-3) ; Sh. Arjun KUchhal ( husband of sister-in-law as  R-4). The Protection of women from Domestic Violence Act,
 2005 would be referred as the Act, 2005.

1 3.

By way of the present order I shall dispose of the interim  order(s) as deemed necessary under S.23(1) of the Act, 2005.
5.
The averments made in the application has mentioned that the  marrioage of the applicant took place on 01.03.2009.
It has  been specifically mentioned that though the arrangements in  the marriage were impressive & imposing the respondents remained unhappy and utterly dissatisfied.
The frequent demands for the dowry started pouring in soon after the marriage.
The agony of the applicant was furthered by the beatings and the ill-treatment in the hands of the said respondents.
The respondent-husband remained unwilling to have physical relationship with the applicant.
The mother-in- law of the applicant often told the respondent No.1 not to sleep with the applicant.
6. As per the averments of the applicant the agonies continued and the husband would very often threaten her with divorce.
Many incidences of irrational behavior on part of the respondent-husband have been averred.
On one occasion the husband drove very recklessly on the roads almost banging the car against the side lane.
On other occasions the husband would behave as a maniac often accompanied by violent outbursts.
The applicant is averred to have been subjected to ruthless beatings.
The applicant has also averred various incidences of physical violence when the respondents have been brutal to the applicant.
The applicant has narrated various incidents where she had subjected to the domestic violence.

The complainant has averred to have been subjected from time to time to the: "physical abuse";
"verbal and emotional abuse"; "economic abuse".
The complainant had been subjected to insults, ridicule, humiliation and name calling.
The complainant has averred deprivation of all economic & financial resources to which the aggrieved person was entitled to.
The application has been supported by an affidavit.

The Present Application U/S. 12 Of The ... vs Unknown on 11 February, 2010 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/89556447/
2 7.
The applicant has also mentioned that she had approached a counselor in order to seek advice.
The respondent-husband is said to have been uncooperative.

in the para No.44 of the application /
compliant that she has learnt from reliable sources that the respondent-husband suffers from a psychiatric disorder.
8. The respondents have not filed any reply to the application of the applicant.
9. The applicant has raised several contentious issues.
At this stage I only need to look at the question whether or not a prima facie case for an 'interim measure' is made out.
The contentious issues could only be decided when the cogent evidence come on record.

At this very stage the Act,
2005 provides for the jurisdiction and powers of the Magistrate to grant the relief(s) which are urgent in nature.

10. The first three paragraphs of the statement of object and reasons under which the Bill No. 116 of 2005 for passing the act was placed before the Parliament, are as under (published in the Gazette of India Extraordinary Part II Section 2 page 22 dated 22nd August, 2005) :-
a. "Domestic violence is undoubtedly a human rights issue and serious deterrent to development.
The Vienna Accord of 1994 and the Beijing Declaration and the Platform for Action (1995) have acknowledged this.

The United Nations Committee on Convention on Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women (CEDAW) in its General Recommendation No. XII (1989) has recommended that State parties should act to protect women against violence of any kind especially that occurring within the family.

entities.text: United Nations Committee on Convention on Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: b. The phenomenon of domestic violence is widely prevalent but has remained largely invisible in the public domain.
Presently, where a woman is subjected to cruelty by her husband or his relatives, it is an offence under Section 498-A of the Indian Penal Code.
The civil law does not however address this phenomenon in its entirety.

c. It is, therefore, proposed to enact a law keeping in view the rights guaranteed under Articles 14, 15 and 21 of the Constitution to provide for a remedy under the civil law which is intended to protect the woman from being victims of domestic violence and to prevent the occurrence of domestic violence in the society."

11. Keeping the above-mentioned objects & reasons in mind to provide for more effective protection of the rights of women guaranteed under the Constitution who are victims of violence of any kind occurring within the family and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto, the bill was presented before the Parliament which has become the Act after passing the same by the Parliament.

Thus, it cannot be lost sight of that the Act has been passed keeping in view the rights guaranteed under Articles 14, 15 and 21 of the Constitution to provide for a remedy under the civil law which is intended to protect the woman from being victims of domestic violence and to prevent the occurrence of domestic violence in the society.
Thus, basically the act has been passed to provide the civil remedy against domestic violence to the women.

The Present Application U/S. 12 Of The ... vs Unknown on 11 February, 2010 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/89556447/
3 12.
I would now deal with the monetary relief sought by the wife.
The application does not disclose the earnings of the respondent-husband.
The application does not even disclose the occupation of the husband.
The whole petition is silent on the financial background of the parties.
The applicant has also sought Rs.20 Lac towards the loss of the earnings.
However, the applicant has not specified what loss of earnings have happened.
The financial background is essential to be considered at the stage of granting of the maintenance.

The term Maintenance as defined in the Advanced Law Lexicon, 3rd Edition 2005 as published by Wadhwa Nagpur includes in all cases, provision for food, clothing, residence, education and medical attendance and treatment.

As per Bouvier Law Dictionary Maintenance is also the means of subsistence, supply of necessaries and conveniences; aid, support, assistance; the support which one person who is bound by law to do so, gives to another for his living.

For computing maintenance the following test have been laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Jasbir Kaur Sehgal v. District Judge, Dehradun and Ors., 1997 (7) SCC 7, wherein it has been observed thus :
'No set formula can be laid for fixing the amount of maintenance.

entities.text: Jasbir Kaur Sehgal v. District Judge, Dehradun and Ors., 1997 (7) SCC 7
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It has, in the very nature of things, to depend on the facts and circumstances of each case.
Some scope for leverage can, however, be always there.

The court has to consider the status of the parties, their respective needs, the capacity of the husband to pay having regard to his reasonable expenses for his own maintenance and of those he is obliged under the law and statutory but involuntary payments or deductions.

The amount of maintenance fixed for the wife should be such as she can live in reasonable comfort considering her status and the mode of life she was used to when she lived with her husband and also that she does not feel handicapped in the prosecution of her case.

At the same time, the amount so fixed cannot be excessive or extortionate."
13.

In 2005 CRI. L. J. 3889 "Gurmeet Kour v. Amrik Singh" the Hon'ble J& K HIGH COURT had observed : "At the time of deciding the question of grant of interim maintenance the Court is not entitled to take into consideration the ultimate possibility of dismissal of main application for grant of maintenance.

entities.text: 2005 CRI. L. J. 3889 "Gurmeet Kour v. Amrik Singh
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The grounds of defense which are subject to the proof cannot be taken into consideration at that stage by the Court."
14. In Bhagwan v. Kamla Devi (AIR 1975 SC 83) it was observed that the wife should be in a position to maintain standard of living which is neither luxurious nor penurious.
15. The applicant has also mentioned about her jewelry articles kept with the respondents.
A list of the jewelry articles is given by the applicant.
The bank accounts of the respondent R-1 and R-2 have been provided.

The respondent R-1 is said to have two bank accounts bearing numbers:
23110559880 (Standard Chattered Bank, Mumbai); and 00011050113475 (HDFC Bank, Mumbai).
The respondent R-2 is said to have a bank account bearing No.00541070000976 at HDFC Bank, Jaipur.
The aspect of the stridhan and its details happens to be a highly contentious issue requiring cogent evidence.
The Present Application U/S. 12 Of The ... vs Unknown on 11 February, 2010 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/89556447/
4 16. At the moment the only aspect that I need to take care of is whether any amount of maintenance can still be granted to the applicant who has only averred the instances of domestic violence.
The question would boil down to the economic independence of the applicant as a woman.

The PWDV Act, 2005 is India's response to the Beijing Declaration which had the objectives such as :
a. Determination to advance the goals of equality, development and peace for all women everywhere in the interest of all humanity, b. Acknowledging the voices of all women everywhere and taking note of the diversity of women and their roles and circumstances, honouring the women who paved the way and inspired by the hope present in the world's youth, c. Recognizing the status of women has advanced in some important respects in the past decade but that progress has been uneven,
inequalities between women and men have persisted and major obstacles remain,
with serious consequences for the well-being of all people, lives of the majority of the world's people, in particular women and children, with origins in both the national and international domains, d. Dedicating unreservedly to addressing these constraints and obstacles and thus enhancing further the advancement and empowerment of women all over the world, and agreeing that this requires urgent action in the spirit of determination, hope, cooperation and solidarity, now and to carry us forward into the next century.
17.

In a report "The Battered Women's Justice Project, Civil Office"
by Christine Thomas (Staff Attorney, BWJP Civil Office, June 2004) it was stated that effective strategies to end violence against women must include strong measures that promote economic security and restitution for survivors.
Many women are compelled to stay in abusive relationships or return to their batterers because of financial constraints and economic concerns.
Moreover, protection order proceedings are an appropriate and necessary venue to address the economic injustice that often characterizes domestic violence.
It is pertinent to acknowledge that even in the most developed countries like the USA there are strong economic provisions for the women.

For instance, child support and/or temporary spousal maintenance awards are specifically authorized by most state statutes; typically, these forms of emergency financial support to survivors and their children can be obtained in protection order proceedings.

The report by Christine Thomas concluded with the remarks:
"Because economic dependence and severe financial stress on abused women can so acutely impact a survivor's choice to stay or leave an abusive relationship and because economic abuse by batterers is often an aspect of the power and control over their lives, stronger legal advocacy for economic safety and restitution is important to the economic empowerment of battered women and the goal of assuring that women may live free of violence and oppression by their intimate partners.
The economic relief available through a protection order may be an essential temporary mechanism to ensure safety and promote economic justice for the survivor."

The Present Application U/S. 12 Of The ... vs Unknown on 11 February, 2010 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/89556447/
5 18.
The legislations meant for the betterment of women though inherently inclined towards the woman will take into account such financial parity.
Justice to women does not squarely mean injustice to men.

But the PWDV Act, 2005, has perceived that a woman needs unique 'economic'
contribution from her husband.

An English novelist Joseph Conrad 1857-1924) had quoted "Being a woman is a terribly difficult task, since it consists principally in dealing with men."
19.

The present case is not yet decided but keeping in view of the background of the Act, 2005 and appreciating that the Act, 2005 is essentially characterized by the 'gender-disposition' towards the women I am less hesitant to hold that the applicant-wife does deserve some 'monetary relief'.

20. In the fact and the circumstances of the present case and after perusing the relevant documents placed by the parties I grant an amount of Rs.20,000/- (Rupees Twenty Thousand) per month to the wife at this stage.
The amount payable is from the date of the filing of the application for the interim maintenance.
As far as the other relief(s) sought by the complainant-wife are concerned they are based on contentious issues and will be considered later at the appropriate (evidence) stage.
The present order is not a comment on the merits of the case.
Disposed of accordingly.
Announced in the open court on this 11th day of February, 2010.
VEENA RANI METROPOLITAN MAGISTRATE: SOUTH DELHI.
